title: Brinks $100M Jewelry Heist: Lead Defendant Pleads GUILTY
summary:
The Brinks jewelry heist explained: on November 19, 2026, Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado, the lead defendant in the July 2022 theft of 24 bags of jewelry from a Brinks semitruck at a truck stop in Lebec, California — jewelry the victims valued at about $100 million, and what federal prosecutors called the largest jewelry heist in U.S. history — pleaded guilty in federal court in Riverside to one count of Hobbs Act robbery (a March 2022 AirTags robbery). His plea agreement admits the heist, his flight to Panama and a string of 2022 cargo thefts; it also records his contention that certain victims had declared a total of less than $10 million to Brinks, which the government disputes. Sentencing is set for April 15, 2027.
Brinks heist, Brinks jewelry heist, $100 million jewelry heist, largest jewelry heist in US history, Lebec truck stop, Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado, guilty plea, Hobbs Act robbery.
Photo: TomasVial, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons (Tocumen International Airport, Panama City; file photo, branding blurred). No photos of the defendant are used.
All co-defendants are presumed innocent; three have pleaded not guilty and their trial is set for March 22, 2027.

question: The victims valued the 24 bags at about $100 million; he contends under $10 million was declared to Brinks. What should he owe? Tell us in the comments.
